svg.text: The 0x800 window row map - which lwSRP attribute row a selection really reaches
GENERATED from milan_datapath.sv (SRP_CTX_ROWS_C = 2*N_STREAMS - 1), endstation_builder.py (ctx_rows_required = L+T-1, SRP_CTX_IDX_BITS) and every configs/endstation_*.yaml.
An attribute row is NOT a stream. Row 0 is the legacy talker+listener PAIR (the LWSRP_* 0x680 group); listener k maps to row k; talker t maps to row (L-1)+t.
So the top row an LxT shape can name is (L-1)+(T-1) and the table must be L+T-1 rows - NOT max(L,T). ctx_idx is 4 bits, so L+T-1 <= 16 caps the fabric.
arty_4x4 - board arty, L=4 listeners, T=4 talkers => 7 attribute rows
the old max(L,T)=4 table ended here - rows 4..6 were refused SILENTLY and aliased row 0
arty_current - board arty, L=1 listeners, T=1 talkers => 1 attribute row
ax7101_8x8 - board ax7101, L=8 listeners, T=8 talkers => 15 attribute rows
the old max(L,T)=8 table ended here - rows 8..14 were refused SILENTLY and aliased row 0
The refusal is now LOUD - which is the whole point of sizing the table from this arithmetic
An out-of-range row is still granted (the port must never hang), but ctx_rd_stat returns 0xDEAD - the window's
"not backed" idiom - instead of row 0's live status, and ctx_oor_o latches into LWSRP_STATUS[11]. On a correctly-sized
build that bit reads 0; a 1 means the shape needs more attribute rows than N_CTX_P provides, which is otherwise
invisible from every counter in the design.
